text:
**Overall:** 6/10. The code is readable, compact, and has a useful test suite, but I would not approve it as-is because the ingest/update logic can silently preserve or overwrite incorrect accounting data.

**Findings:**

| Severity | File | Lines | Issue |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| high | `jobwatch/db.py` | 70-84 | Equal-rank terminal states can overwrite newer final records with older terminal records, corrupting job state and usage data. |
| high | `jobwatch/db.py` | 74-80 | “Unchanged” detection compares only state/end/elapsed, so later dumps with corrected user/partition/CPU/GPU/exit-code data are skipped. |
| medium | `jobwatch/parser.py`, `jobwatch/reports.py` | 118-125, 58-70, 113-121 | Offset-aware timestamps are stored and compared as raw text, so SQLite ordering/filtering can be wrong across time zones. |
| medium | `jobwatch/parser.py` | 148-163 | Negative `AllocCPUS` or GPU counts are accepted, allowing negative CPU/GPU-hours in reports. |
| medium | `jobwatch/parser.py` | 152-164 | Empty user, partition, and exit code fields are accepted and stored, producing blank report groups and weak data quality. |
| medium | `jobwatch/reports.py` | 58-68, 95-104, 135-147 | Report queries scan the whole table and compute `COALESCE(end,start,submit)` per row with no index strategy, which will degrade on real accounting history. |
| low | `jobwatch/cli.py` | 99-103, 122-126, 139-143, 176-180 | SQLite/open/report errors are not caught, so common DB path or corruption failures surface as tracebacks instead of CLI errors. |
| low | `jobwatch/parser.py` | 167-190 | File parsing is all-or-nothing for header recognition and exact field layout, with no tolerance for harmless exported-column variation. |

**Lines to rewrite/significantly change:** about 120 production lines, mostly in `db.py`, `parser.py`, and `reports.py`, plus targeted tests for stale/equal-rank updates, corrected resource data, timestamp offsets, and invalid resource counts.

**PR approval:** No.

Tests run: `pytest -q` passed, 61 tests. There was one pytest cache warning because the environment could not write `.pytest_cache`.

issues.description: Equal-rank terminal states can overwrite newer final records with older terminal records.
Unchanged detection ignores corrected user, partition, CPU, GPU, and exit-code fields.
Offset-aware timestamps are stored and compared as raw text, causing incorrect ordering across time zones.
Negative CPU or GPU allocation values are accepted and can produce negative usage totals.
Empty user, partition, and exit-code fields are accepted without validation.
Report queries perform full scans with computed reference-time filtering and no supporting indexes.
SQLite and report errors surface as tracebacks instead of user-facing CLI errors.
Parser requires an exact header and field layout, making ingestion brittle to harmless sacct export variation.
